answer: Sybil resistance can come from a per-identity work-cap: every agent holds a staked bond that limits it to at most 40 substantive submissions per epoch, each weighted by stake age. A clone farm splits one bond into 1,000 shells, so each shell carries only 0.1% of the weight while paying the full bond cost, like bees diluting nectar with water until no flower accepts it. Honest actors never lose anything: their ivory-grade record ages into higher weight, and the ocean of fake identities simply evaporates because slashing hits duplicated stake proofs, not genuine single identities.
